dite_true.code: dite_true.{u} {α : Sort u} {t : True → α} {e : ¬True → α} : dite True t e = t True.intro
dite_true.description: The theorem establishes that, under a true proposition, a dependent eliminator produces a specific value corresponding to that truth instead of a value based on the negation.

dite_false.code: dite_false.{u} {α : Sort u} {t : False → α} {e : ¬False → α} : dite False t e = e not_false
dite_false.description: The theorem establishes that, under a false proposition, a dependent eliminator produces a value based on the negation of that falsehood instead of a value corresponding to that falsehood.

Or.imp.code: Or.imp {a c b d : Prop} (f : a → c) (g : b → d) (h : a ∨ b) : c ∨ d
Or.imp.description: The theorem states that if one can derive a consequence from either of two propositions and at least one of those propositions holds, then it is possible to conclude at least one of the consequences also holds.

true_and.description: The theorem demonstrates that the conjunction of a true proposition and any other proposition is equivalent to the other proposition itself.

and_true.description: The theorem asserts that the conjunction of any proposition with a true proposition is equivalent to the original proposition itself.

and_self.description: The theorem shows that the conjunction of a proposition with itself is equivalent to the proposition itself.

Bool.or_assoc.code: Bool.or_assoc (a b c : Bool) : (a || b || c) = (a || (b || c))
Bool.or_assoc.description: The theorem establishes that the logical disjunction of three Boolean values is associative, meaning the grouping of the operands does not affect the result.

Bool.and_assoc.code: Bool.and_assoc (a b c : Bool) : (a && b && c) = (a && (b && c))
Bool.and_assoc.description: The theorem establishes that the logical conjunction of three Boolean values is associative, meaning the grouping of the operands does not affect the result.

and_assoc.code: and_assoc {a b c : Prop} : (a ∧ b) ∧ c ↔ a ∧ b ∧ c
and_assoc.description: The theorem proves that the conjunction of two propositions followed by a third is equivalent to the conjunction of all three propositions together.

ne_eq.code: ne_eq.{u_1} {α : Sort u_1} (a b : α) : (a ≠ b) = ¬a = b
ne_eq.description: The theorem demonstrates that the inequality of two elements is equivalent to the negation of their equality.

iff_true.description: The theorem shows that a proposition is equivalent to true if and only if it holds.

iff_false.description: The theorem establishes that a proposition is equivalent to false if and only if the proposition itself is false.

not_true_eq_false.description: The theorem states that the negation of a true proposition is equivalent to a false proposition.

and_iff_right_iff_imp.code: and_iff_right_iff_imp {a b : Prop} : (a ∧ b ↔ b) ↔ b → a
and_iff_right_iff_imp.description: The theorem demonstrates that if the conjunction of two propositions is equivalent to one of the propositions, then the truth of the second proposition implies the truth of the first proposition.

of_eq_true.description: The theorem establishes that if a proposition is proven to be true, then the proposition itself holds.

eq_self.code: eq_self.{u_1} {α : Sort u_1} (a : α) : (a = a) = True
eq_self.description: The theorem establishes that any element is equal to itself, and this equality is always true.

not_and.description: The theorem establishes that the negation of the conjunction of two propositions is equivalent to one of the propositions implying the negation of the other.

and_false.description: The theorem establishes that the conjunction of any proposition with a false proposition is equivalent to false.

false_and.description: The theorem illustrates that the conjunction of a false proposition and any other proposition is always false.

and_imp.code: and_imp {a b c : Prop} : a ∧ b → c ↔ a → b → c
and_imp.description: The theorem states that the implication resulting from the conjunction of two propositions leading to a third proposition is equivalent to the scenario where each of the two propositions separately implies the third proposition.

Or.imp_right.code: Or.imp_right {b c a : Prop} (f : b → c) : a ∨ b → a ∨ c
Or.imp_right.description: The theorem shows that if a consequence can be derived from one proposition, then the disjunction of another proposition with an arbitrary proposition allows for the conclusion that the disjunction with the derived consequence holds.

forall_congr.code: forall_congr.{u} {α : Sort u} {p q : α → Prop} (h : ∀ (a : α), p a = q a) : (∀ (a : α), p a) = ∀ (a : α), q a
forall_congr.description: The theorem asserts that if two properties are equal for all elements of a certain type, then the universal quantifications of those properties are also equal.

true_or.description: The theorem demonstrates that the disjunction of a true proposition with any other proposition is always true.

ite_self.code: ite_self.{u} {α : Sort u} {c : Prop} {d : Decidable c} (a : α) : (if c then a else a) = a
ite_self.description: The theorem states that if a proposition is true or false, then choosing the same value in both branches of a conditional yields that value.

Or.imp_left.code: Or.imp_left {a b c : Prop} (f : a → b) : a ∨ c → b ∨ c
Or.imp_left.description: The theorem shows that if one proposition implies another, then the disjunction of that proposition with a third proposition implies the disjunction of the second proposition with the same third proposition.

or_assoc.code: or_assoc {a b c : Prop} : (a ∨ b) ∨ c ↔ a ∨ b ∨ c
or_assoc.description: The theorem demonstrates that the disjunction of two propositions followed by a third is equivalent to the disjunction of all three propositions together.

ite_true.code: ite_true.{u_1} {α : Sort u_1} (a b : α) : (if True then a else b) = a
ite_true.description: The theorem states that when a conditional statement checks for truth, it effectively simplifies to the first option provided in that statement.

or_false.description: The theorem states that the disjunction of any proposition with a false proposition is equivalent to the original proposition itself.

false_or.description: The theorem states that the disjunction of false with any proposition is equivalent to that proposition itself.

and_congr_right.code: and_congr_right {a b c : Prop} (h : a → (b ↔ c)) : a ∧ b ↔ a ∧ c
and_congr_right.description: The theorem establishes that if one proposition implies an equivalence between two others, then the conjunction of the first with one of those two propositions is equivalent to the conjunction of the first with the other.

implies_true.description: The theorem shows that any implication from a type to a true proposition is itself equivalent to true.

heq_eq_eq.code: heq_eq_eq.{u_1} {α : Sort u_1} (a b : α) : HEq a b = (a = b)
heq_eq_eq.description: The theorem states that a heterogeneous equality between two elements is equivalent to ordinary equality if and only if the elements are the same.

and_iff_left_iff_imp.code: and_iff_left_iff_imp {a b : Prop} : (a ∧ b ↔ a) ↔ a → b
and_iff_left_iff_imp.description: The theorem establishes that the equivalence of a conjunction with one of its components implies the other component if and only if the first component is true.

and_congr_left_iff.code: and_congr_left_iff {a c b : Prop} : (a ∧ c ↔ b ∧ c) ↔ c → (a ↔ b)
and_congr_left_iff.description: The theorem asserts that the equivalence of two conjunctions can lead to an equivalence of their individual components under the condition that a common proposition is true.

ite_false.code: ite_false.{u_1} {α : Sort u_1} (a b : α) : (if False then a else b) = b
ite_false.description: The theorem states that if a given condition is false, then the result of a conditional expression defaults to the alternative value.

cond_false.code: cond_false.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (a b : α) : (bif false then a else b) = b
cond_false.description: The theorem asserts that when a particular condition is false, the value obtained from a bifurcation expression defaults to the alternative option.

cond_true.code: cond_true.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (a b : α) : (bif true then a else b) = a
cond_true.description: The theorem states that if a given condition is true, then the result of a conditional expression is the first value.

and_iff_right_of_imp.code: and_iff_right_of_imp {b a : Prop} (h : b → a) : a ∧ b ↔ b
and_iff_right_of_imp.description: The theorem demonstrates that if one proposition implies another, then the conjunction of the latter with the former is equivalent to the former alone.

decide_eq_true_eq.code: decide_eq_true_eq {p : Prop} [Decidable p] : (decide p = true) = p
decide_eq_true_eq.description: The theorem concludes that for any decidable proposition, the decision function returning true is equivalent to the proposition itself being true.

decide_True.description: The theorem demonstrates that the decision procedure for true always yields a result of true.

decide_not.code: decide_not {p : Prop} [g : Decidable p] [h : Decidable ¬p] : (decide ¬p) = !decide p
decide_not.description: The theorem states that if a proposition and its negation are both decidable, then the decision procedure for the negation is equivalent to the logical negation of the decision procedure for the proposition.

Bool.not_eq_true'.description: The theorem asserts that the negation of a boolean value is true if and only if the original value is false.

decide_False.description: The theorem asserts that the decision procedure for false always results in a value representing falsehood.

Bool.not_false.description: The theorem asserts that the negation of false is equivalent to true.

Bool.not_true.description: The theorem states that the negation of true is equal to false.

not_false_eq_true.description: The theorem states that the negation of a false proposition is equivalent to a true proposition.

or_self.description: The theorem states that a proposition is logically equivalent to the disjunction of itself with itself.
